subject: Cross-border transfer playbook & procurement check-in (MediSolve)
messages:
From: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@medisolve.com>

Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medisolve.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Transfer questions & initial playbook request

Hi David —

Thanks for taking the time during last week's demo. Legal and procurement asked me to reach out with a focused list of questions so we can align on signing timelines. Key asks:

- Which transfer mechanisms do you expect to rely on for our EU user data if we proceed with Redwood Hosted API? SCCs + UK IDTA/UK Addendum or reliance on TIA/DTIA?
- We need a clear mapping of subprocessors (full list + data access levels) and whether any processing happens outside the EU/UK.
- For regulated workflows we run token caching on-prem — can you confirm onshore fallback / cache residency options and audit logging evidence?
- Procurement also asked for a sample DPA with explicit redline fields they typically require (LIABILITY cap, data retention, incident SLA).

I've attached our initial questionnaire (MediSolve_transfer_questions.pdf). Can we set a 30–45 minute call early next week to go through? Sanjay will join from Legal.

Best,
Claire
Head of Legal — Medisolve Inc

Attachment: MediSolve_transfer_questions.pdf (PDF, 2 pages)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@medisolve.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medisolve.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 22 Aug 2026 12:03:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Transfer questions & initial playbook request

Claire — thanks for the detailed list and the questionnaire. High level answers below; I'll propose a call time in a follow-up.

Short answers up front:
- Hosted API: default transfer path is SCCs (EU Commission standard clauses) plus our UK Addendum / IDTA for UK-to-third-country transfers. For customers with strict residency requirements, we can deploy with dedicated onshore capacity or provide documented fallback behaviors (see caching note).
- Subprocessors: we maintain a live subprocessor page that we can export and attest to in the DPA; we'll provide access to the latest CSV and the security attestations for major infra providers.
- Cache/onshore fallback: we support prefix/KV cache pinning to dedicated onshore instances in Dedicated + Private modes; for Hosted we offer documented cache residency options and event-level audit logs.
- DPA redlines: we have a standard Redwood_DPA_v3; procurement positions typically start there. We can accept targeted changes on liability, data retention, and SLA with account-level exceptions documented in the addendum.

I'll attach the standard DPA draft and loop in Kimberly for technical evidence and Laura for procurement cadence. Proposed times for a 30-min call next Tue/Wed (we're flexible EMEA mornings).

Thanks,
David Kim
Head of Privacy & Trust — Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_DPA_v3_redlines.docx (DOCX, 4 pages)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Claire Thompson <claire.thompson@medisolve.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medisolve.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 Aug 2026 08:10:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Transfer questions & initial playbook request — technical evidence

Hi all — adding some implementation-level detail so Medisolve can map requirements to artifacts quickly. Short bullets:

- Transfer mechanism: Redwood typically layers SCCs + UK IDTA (addendum) for cross-border exports. Operationally we maintain a transfer impact assessment (DTIA) for each model and a separate TIA for telemetry + logs.
- Subprocessors: current hosted infra subprocessors include cloud provider compute (region-specific), observability vendor (no customer PII), and model distribution partners. We provide CSV export with column-level access: processor_name, region_of_processing, processing_purposes, access_scope, SOC2_report_link.
- Evidence we can provide next week:
  * SOC 2 type II (redacted) — 2025 cycle
  * Data flow diagram (per-account) — PNG/PDF
  * DTIA_scope_matrix.xlsx (attached) — maps data categories to transfer mechanisms and compensating controls
  * Audit-log sample (anonymized) — demonstrates request-level routing timestamps
- Cache residency: for Hosted customers we document an onshore cache fallback plan (not guaranteed unless Dedicated). For Medisolve use-case, we recommend: Dedicated capacity in EU region with token prefix pinning + KV encryption-at-rest and keying via your KMS (bring-your-own-key supported for Private).

Next steps I suggest:
1) We complete the DTIA_scope_matrix with MediSolve's data categories (I can pre-fill with assumptions from your questionnaire).
2) Review DPA redlines and surface critical must-haves (Procurement).
3) Live call to confirm evidence artifacts and DocuSign timeline.

Attachment: DTIA_scope_matrix.xlsx (XLSX, 1 sheet)

—Kimberly
Principal Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
